article.title: Put off
article.description: Meaning: to postpone or delay something. Example: 'We had to put off the meeting until next week.' Grammar note: separable — 'put the meeting off' is also correct. Second meaning: to make someone dislike something — 'The bad reviews put me off that restaurant.'

slides.headlineRest: — Two Meanings You Need to Know
slides.body: The versatile phrasal verb 'put off' carries two distinct meanings. Firstly, it means to postpone or delay something. For example, 'We had to put off the meeting until next week.' Keep in mind that 'put off' is separable, so 'put the meeting off' is also grammatically correct. Secondly, 'put off' can mean to make someone dislike something or lose interest. For instance, 'The bad reviews put me off that restaurant.'
